title: Smoothness from Artinian tests with the fixed residue field
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $Y$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $x\in X$ and $k=\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. A small extension is a surjection $B'\twoheadrightarrow B$ of Artinian local commutative rings whose kernel has module length one, equivalently is one-dimensional over the residue field of $B'$ and is annihilated by its maximal ideal. Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize; local means that there is a unique maximal ideal. Suppose that for every small extension of these rings with residue fields identified with $k$, every map $a:\operatorname{Spec}B\to X$ restricting on $\operatorname{Spec}k$ to the canonical point $x$, and every $b:\operatorname{Spec}B'\to Y$ with $fa=b\operatorname{Spec}(B'\to B)$, there is $a':\operatorname{Spec}B'\to X$ satisfying $a'\operatorname{Spec}(B'\to B)=a$ and $fa'=b$. Here all ring maps respect the residue-field identifications and affine spectra are [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then there is an open subscheme $N\subseteq X$ containing $x$ such that $f|_N:N\to Y$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

source.place: Tag 02HX (lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point), implication (4) to (1); small extensions are Tag 02HS (algebra.tex, definition-small-extension).

proof.text: Choose $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Y$ containing $f(x)$ from a Noetherian affine cover in [pqf-def-locnoeth]. From the finite-type affine cover in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], choose $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq f^{-1}V$ containing $x$, with $A$ finitely generated over $R$. Factor the restriction through $V$. Write $\mathfrak q$ for the prime of $A$ corresponding to $x$ and identify $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\kappa(x)=k$.

Consider a small extension $\varphi:B'\to B$ with residues identified with $k$, and maps $\rho:R\to B'$, $a:A\to B$ with $a\circ(R\to A)=\varphi\rho$ and $A\to B\to k$ the canonical residue map at $\mathfrak q$. The affine spectrum correspondence gives a test square in $X,Y$. Its restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is exactly $x$, so the hypothesis supplies a lift into $X$. By the unique-prime lemma $\operatorname{Spec}B'$ has one point; the lift sends it to $x$, since its restriction along $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}B'$ is the original map. It therefore factors through $U$. Uniqueness of factorization through $V$ and the affine spectrum correspondence give an $R$-compatible ring lift $A\to B'$. This proves precisely the fixed-residue ring lifting hypothesis of the next step.

source.place: 02HX (lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point), factor test maps and lifts into the chosen affines

proof.text: Choose finitely many $R$-algebra generators of $A$ and evaluate to obtain a surjection $\alpha:P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_d]\to A$. Set $Q=\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, $C=P_Q$, and $S=A_{\mathfrak q}$. The induced map $C\to S$ is surjective: lift the numerator and denominator of a fraction in $S$ along $\alpha$; the lifted denominator lies outside $Q$. The finite-type Noetherian theorem and localization theorem make $C$ Noetherian; localization at $Q$ makes it local. Write $J=\ker(C\to S)$ and $\mathfrak m=QC$.

Apply [lem-sfb-fixed-residue-lifts-truncated-section] to $R,A,\mathfrak q,C\to S$ and the ring lifting property proved in step 2. For every $N\ge1$ this gives an $R$-algebra section of $C/(J^2+\mathfrak m^N)\to C/(J+\mathfrak m^N)$. In particular no lift with a larger residue field has been assumed.

source.place: 02HT (lemma-smooth-test-artinian), truncated quotients and successive application of (4)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-truncated-polynomial-sections-smooth] to the finite polynomial presentation of step 3 and the sections of step 4. Obtain $g\notin\mathfrak q$ for which $R\to A_g$ is smooth.

The principal-localization open immersion identifies $\operatorname{Spec}A_g$ with $D(g)\subseteq U$, which contains $x$. The affine smoothness comparison makes $\operatorname{Spec}A_g\to V$ smooth. Compose with the open inclusion $V\to Y$ and transport along this identification, using smoothness under restriction and isomorphism, to obtain a smooth morphism $f|_{D(g)}:D(g)\to Y$. Since $U$ is open in $X$, $D(g)$ is the required open neighbourhood $N$ in $X$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q03-0c190a90b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the source in more-morphisms.tex 02HX (all four conditions and the affine reduction) and the full proof of (4)⇒(1) of algebra.tex 02HT. The item statement is the same as the live node, and it is 02HX (4)⇒(1) with the residue field fixed to κ(x). Its citers use exactly that statement. I tested it on F_p(s^{1/p}) over F_p(s) with B'=F_p(s)[u]/((u^p−s)^2): there is no lift, so the test catches the inseparable non-smooth case, as it should. Step 1 picks U inside f^{-1}V; def-weil-finite-type-morphism allows this because it is stated for every affine V. Step 2 turns the ring test into the scheme test. The one-point Spec B' maps to x, so the lift factors through U, and uniqueness of the factorization through V gives R-compatibility. Steps 3–6 match 02HT and the cited statements say what the steps take from them. proof_deps is exactly the union of the steps' uses. New node 1 (fixed-residue lifts → truncated sections) is true by the 02HT filtration argument. The residue maps stay identities at each stage, so the fixed-residue test applies at every step. N=1 and E=F are trivial. It strictly strengthens the existing lem-weil-pbc-artinian-lifting-truncated-section, which assumes the stronger arbitrary-residue tests, so it is not a duplicate. New node 2 (truncated sections → A_g smooth) is true: Artin–Rees, then lem-weil-pbc-truncated-section-conormal-residue-kernel, then split injection and IsSmoothAt. No existing node states it. It has no lifting hypothesis, so it is strictly smaller than the item. The two nodes are of comparable size and the item proof is a short assembly of them. Both are statement-only, self-contained, and have correct sources and created metadata. Nothing cites SGA. I accept the tool_use lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine (generic affine smoothness comparison). No changes made.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_near_of_fixed_residue_artinian_lifting {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (x : X) (hlift : ∀ (B' B : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsArtinianRing B'] [IsArtinianRing B] [IsLocalRing B'] [IsLocalRing B] (q : B' ⟶ B), Function.Surjective q.hom → Module.length B' (RingHom.ker q.hom) = 1 → ∀ (r : B ⟶ X.residueField x), Function.Surjective r.hom → ∀ (a : Spec B ⟶ X) (b : Spec B' ⟶ Y), Spec.map r ≫ a = X.fromSpecResidueField x → a ≫ f = Spec.map q ≫ b → ∃ a' : Spec B' ⟶ X, Spec.map q ≫ a' = a ∧ a' ≫ f = b) : ∃ N : X.Opens, x ∈ N ∧ Smooth (N.ι ≫ f)
